newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania says worried by Belarus events.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania says worried by Belarus events.

text.p: The Baltic state of Lithuania said on Monday it was worried about events in neighbouring Belarus, where President Alexander Lukashenko is facing growing political opposition to his plans to increase his powers.

About 1,000 Belarussians rallied outside parliament, calling on deputies to impeach Lukashenko, who also faced a mutiny within the normally loyal government. A similar protest outside parliament ended in clashes with police on Sunday.

"The ministry of foreign affairs of the Republic of Lithuania expresses its concern about the course of events and the constantly worsening political situation in Belarus," the ministry said in a statement.

Lithuania shares a long border with Belarus and several opposition newspapers are printed in Vilnius, some 20,000 of which were reported by Lithuanian newspaper Respublika to have been seized on Friday night by Belarus customs.
The foreign ministry said it wanted to maintain good relations with Belarus and see it develop as a European state in a "legal and democratic" way.
"...we urge the solving of the problems which have arisen in Belarus through the dialogue of the authorities, strictly adhering to the principles of democracy and human rights," the statement added.
It said that universally recognised constitutional principles could be found to solve the situation.
